question: Harishena was the court poet of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Samudragupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Harishena was the **court poet of Samudragupta**, one of the most illustrious rulers of the Gupta Empire.
 
• He composed the **Allahabad Pillar Inscription**, which provides detailed accounts of Samudragupta's conquests and achievements.
 
• The Allahabad Pillar Inscription is written in Sanskrit and consists of poetic verses in the **classical kavya style**.
 
• Harishena depicted Samudragupta as a **great warrior, statesman, and patron of arts**, earning him the title of "Napoleon of India."
 
• The inscription highlights Samudragupta's military campaigns, administrative prowess, and cultural contributions during his reign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gupta Empire:** The Gupta Empire (circa 320–550 CE) is considered a golden age of Indian culture, art, science, and literature.
 
• **Samudragupta:** Known for his military campaigns, he expanded the Gupta Empire significantly and established dominance over northern and central India.
 
• **Allahabad Pillar Inscription:** This inscription is a primary source for understanding the history and achievements of Samudragupta, written by his court poet Harishena.
 
• **Classical Kavya Style:** A refined poetic style in ancient Sanskrit literature, characterized by intricate wordplay, metaphors, and rhythmic structure.
 
• **Patronage of Arts:** Samudragupta was a celebrated patron of arts and culture, fostering advancements in music, poetry, and sculpture during his reign.
